gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-runic: Wide-spaced and wiry, Bushcraft draws every curve without a swell, while Noto Sans Runic keeps a big x-height and open curves. Expressive lettering against a quiet, tidy body is the draw.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-samari: Noto Sans Samaritan reads generously, its hefty lowercase full of daylight inside each curve, while Bushcraft spaces its closed letters wide. Closed against open is the whole story here.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-sc: Expressive and a bit like glass tubing, Bushcraft keeps a hollow, constant line and wide spacing between characters. Noto Sans SC then settles into sans-serif text with short ascenders, which should read steadily over pages.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-sharad: Noto Sans Sharada has bulky lowercase and open, never-closed round letters. Beneath the wide-set Bushcraft heading, whole paragraphs of text should feel sturdy and quite unfussy rather than dense.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-sundan: Clean and open, Noto Sans Sundanese gives its e crossbars open mouths and keeps capitals near lowercase height. But Bushcraft closes its letters and spreads them wide, so the body font is best left at a generous size.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Taut as drawn string, Bushcraft sets its letters far apart. Noto Sans Syriac brings tall, bulb-like bowls and easy s turns, so paragraphs of text should read in a friendly, modern way.

Noto Sans Syriac Western reads sturdy, like bundled cable. Bushcraft draws closed, wire-like letters with generous spacing, so running text in the body font should feel modern and clean, terminals held back.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-tagban: Expressive and wide-set, Bushcraft draws closed letters with no vertical emphasis and no horizontal thinning. And Noto Sans Tagbanwa fills most of the height with open curves, so extended reading should feel clean.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-tai-vi: Smooth as a pen plotter, Bushcraft spaces its constant-weight letters wide, while Noto Sans Tai Viet stays short on ascenders. Expressive flair above a restrained, tall-x-height body is the draw.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-takri: Bushcraft gives every stroke equal visual weight in closed, widely spaced letters, while Noto Sans Takri leaves its round forms open. One shows off expression; the other quietly carries the text.
